name: Ribbon
rootCause: Six days before the exploit, Ribbon Finance (operating as Aevo) deployed an oracle infrastructure update to its legacy DeFi Options Vaults (DOVs) on Ethereum. The update introduced two critical flaws: first, the oracle proxy permitted any address — not just authorized parties — to set expiry prices for newly created option series, effectively removing access control on a price-writing function; second, the update standardized oracle precision to 18 decimal places for newer tokens while older supported assets still used 8 decimal places, creating an exploitable arithmetic mismatch. The attacker created multiple minimal-collateral accounts, minted a large number of oTokens against them, then called the permissionless expiry-price setter to inject arbitrary prices at a shared expiration timestamp. With no maximum payout caps enforced per account or per option series, the attacker drained approximately $2.7 million from the legacy DOV vaults. Aevo subsequently proposed repaying active users with a 19% haircut using funds from dormant accounts. In December 2025, the legacy Ribbon Finance (now Aevo) Ethereum options vaults were exploited for around $2.7 million following an oracle infrastructure upgrade that left expiry price-setting permissions unprotected. An attacker manipulated expiry prices of vault assets, draining reserves before the vaults were permanently decommissioned. Aevo's main derivatives exchange and non-vault user funds were not affected. A December 6, 2025 oracle proxy upgrade for legacy Ribbon vaults removed access control checks on the expiry price-setting function for new assets, allowing anyone to push arbitrary expiry prices.
